faq.ue.title: UE Manila Program and Contact
faq.a1: Computer Engineering combines principles from electrical engineering and computer science to develop computing systems that integrate hardware and software.
faq.q2: How is Computer Engineering different from Computer Science?
faq.a2: Computer Engineering commonly emphasizes hardware-software integration, while Computer Science commonly emphasizes software, algorithms, data, and computing theory. The subjects overlap, and the balance varies by program.
faq.q3: Does Computer Engineering involve both hardware and software?
faq.a3: Yes. Computer Engineering connects physical computing components with the software that controls and uses them.
faq.q4: Is programming part of Computer Engineering?
faq.q8: What careers can Computer Engineering graduates explore?
faq.a8: Graduates may explore roles involving embedded systems, hardware, software, networks, cybersecurity, systems integration, data, cloud computing, robotics, technical support, and research.
faq.q9: Does BS Computer Engineering have a dedicated PRC licensure examination?
faq.a9: No. BS Computer Engineering does not have its own dedicated Professional Regulation Commission licensure examination.
faq.q10: Which program and campus does this website represent?
faq.q11: What is the approved accreditation status shown for UE Manila BS Computer Engineering?
faq.a11: UE Manila BS Computer Engineering holds PACUCOA Level II Reaccredited Status, valid until November 2027.
faq.q12: Where can I confirm current admissions or program information?
faq.a12: Use the Contact page for verified Dean's Office details for program inquiries, and confirm admissions information through UE Manila's official channels.

whatIs.hwsw.integration.title: Where They Meet: Hardware-Software Integration
whatIs.hwsw.integration.desc: The defining skill of a Computer Engineer is co-design — making hardware and software decisions together to optimize for performance, power, cost, and reliability. This systems-level thinking is what distinguishes Computer Engineering from its parent disciplines.
whatIs.fields.intro: Computer Engineering spans multiple interconnected fields. Students typically build depth in one or more of these areas through electives, projects, and research.
whatIs.fields.item1.topics: Key topics: Microcontrollers, RTOS, C/C++, bare-metal programming
whatIs.fields.item1.apps: Applications: Automotive ECUs, medical devices, IoT sensors, industrial controllers
whatIs.fields.item2.topics: Key topics: ISA design, pipelining, cache hierarchy, parallel processing
whatIs.fields.item2.apps: Applications: CPU/GPU design, high-performance computing, accelerator chips
whatIs.fields.item3.topics: Key topics: Verilog/VHDL, FPGA, ASIC flow, timing analysis
whatIs.fields.item3.apps: Applications: Custom SoCs, AI accelerators, memory controllers, I/O interfaces
whatIs.fields.item4.topics: Key topics: TCP/IP, routing, switching, network security, QoS
whatIs.fields.item4.apps: Applications: Data centers, 5G/6G, IoT connectivity, SDN/NFV
whatIs.fields.item5.topics: Key topics: DSP algorithms, filters, transforms, real-time processing
whatIs.fields.item5.apps: Applications: Wireless comms, audio/video codecs, radar/sonar, biomedical imaging
whatIs.fields.item6.topics: Key topics: Control theory, sensor fusion, ROS, real-time control loops
whatIs.fields.item6.apps: Applications: Industrial robots, autonomous vehicles, drones, surgical robots
whatIs.do.intro: Computer Engineers work across the full lifecycle of computing systems. Their work typically spans these core activities:
whatIs.do.note: Note: The specific mix of activities varies by role. Computer Engineering's breadth allows graduates to specialize based on interest.
whatIs.vsCS.title: Computer Engineering vs. Computer Science
whatIs.vsCS.intro: Both disciplines work with computing, but they differ in focus and scope:
whatIs.vsCS.row1.cpe: Hardware–software interface; systems that integrate both
whatIs.vsCS.row2.cpe: Often emphasizes circuits, architecture, digital logic, and hardware-software integration
whatIs.vsCS.row2.cs: Coverage varies by program and may include architecture and hardware-related topics
whatIs.vsCS.row3.cs: Broad: applications, systems, web, AI/ML, theory
whatIs.vsCS.row4.cpe: Often includes both continuous and discrete mathematics
whatIs.vsCS.row4.cs: Often emphasizes discrete mathematics while requirements vary by program
whatIs.vsCS.row5.cpe: Chips, boards, embedded devices, real-time systems
whatIs.vsCS.conclusion: In practice, the fields overlap significantly. Computer Engineers may work extensively with software, and Computer Scientists may work with hardware. The emphasis of either degree varies by institution and curriculum.

spec.data.apps.title: Example Applications

spec.robotics.apps.title: Example Applications

faq.careers.title: Careers
faq.a4: Yes. Programming supports work in areas such as embedded systems, firmware, system software, automation, and hardware-software integration.
faq.q5: Is Computer Engineering only about building computers?
faq.a5: No. The field also covers computing systems found in devices, networks, automation, communications, and many other applications.
faq.q6: What areas can Computer Engineering students explore?
faq.a6: General areas include embedded systems, computer architecture, networks, cybersecurity, robotics, software development, and hardware design. Available subjects vary by institution and curriculum.
faq.q7: What skills are useful when studying Computer Engineering?
faq.a7: Logical thinking, problem solving, communication, mathematics, and a willingness to learn both programming and electronics are useful foundations.
